question: Your CI pipeline uses Claude Code to review pull requests in three categories: security, null-handling bugs, and naming conventions. A spot check of last month's findings shows false-positive rates of 6% for security, 9% for null-handling, and 68% for naming conventions, while security produces the most findings overall. Developers on several teams have now muted the review bot entirely. Which change should you make first?

options.text: Temporarily disable the security category because it produces the most findings, and keep the null-handling and naming-convention categories active.
options.reason: Finding volume is not the cause; the noisy naming category stays active and keeps undermining trust, and accurate security findings are lost.

options.text: Temporarily disable the naming-convention category and keep security and null-handling active, then re-enable naming after its rewritten criteria pass testing.
options.reason: Temporarily disabling the one high false-positive category restores developer trust in the accurate categories while you improve the prompt for that category.

options.text: Keep all three categories active, and add an instruction telling Claude to be conservative and report only naming issues it is sure about.
options.reason: The guide says general instructions like "be conservative" fail to improve precision compared to specific categorical criteria.

options.text: Replace the naming-convention category with a broader code-style category that also covers formatting, comment wording, and file layout.
options.reason: A broader, vaguer category moves away from explicit criteria, keeps noisy findings reaching developers, and does nothing to restore their trust.
